# package opcua

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua"
```

Package opcua provides a high-level OPC-UA client and server implementation in pure Go.

The root package contains the [Client](#type-client) for connecting to OPC-UA servers and performing read, write, browse, subscribe, and method call operations.

#### Client Usage {#hdr-Client_Usage}

Create a client and connect:

	c, err := opcua.NewClient("opc.tcp://localhost:4840",
	    opcua.SecurityFromEndpoint(ep, ua.UserTokenTypeAnonymous),
	    opcua.CertificateFile("client-cert.pem"),
	    opcua.PrivateKeyFile("client-key.pem"),
	    opcua.TrustedCertificates(serverCA),
	)
	if err != nil {
	    log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := c.Connect(ctx); err != nil {
	    log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer c.Close(ctx)

Read a value:

	dv, err := c.ReadValue(ctx, ua.NewNumericNodeID(0, 2258))

Subscribe to changes:

	sub, ch, err := c.NewSubscription().
	    Interval(100 * time.Millisecond).
	    Monitor(nodeID).
	    Start(ctx)

#### Sub-packages {#hdr-Sub_packages}

The server package provides the OPC-UA server implementation. The ua package defines all OPC-UA data types and service messages. The uasc package implements the Secure Conversation layer. The uacp package implements the Connection Protocol (TCP transport). The uapolicy package implements the security policies.

### func NewDataChangeFilter

```go
func NewDataChangeFilter(trigger ua.DataChangeTrigger, deadbandType ua.DeadbandType, deadbandValue float64) *ua.ExtensionObject
```

NewDataChangeFilter returns a DataChangeFilter (Part 4 §7.22.2) wrapped for use as [ua.MonitoringParameters](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#MonitoringParameters).Filter of a monitored item on the Value attribute:

	req := opcua.NewMonitoredItemCreateRequestWithDefaults(nodeID, ua.AttributeIDValue, 1)
	req.RequestedParameters.Filter = opcua.NewDataChangeFilter(
	    ua.DataChangeTriggerStatusValue, ua.DeadbandTypeAbsolute, 0.5)

trigger selects what counts as a change (status only, status or value, or status, value or source timestamp). deadbandType and deadbandValue suppress value changes that stay within the deadband of the last reported value: [ua.DeadbandTypeAbsolute](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#DeadbandTypeAbsolute) takes the absolute change, [ua.DeadbandTypePercent](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#DeadbandTypePercent) a percentage (0–100) of the node's EURange, and [ua.DeadbandTypeNone](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#DeadbandTypeNone) ignores deadbandValue. A deadband needs a numeric variable; the server answers the item with a Bad status when it cannot apply the filter.

### func SelectEndpoint

```go
func SelectEndpoint(endpoints []*ua.EndpointDescription, policy string, mode ua.MessageSecurityMode, certificate []byte) (*ua.EndpointDescription, error)
```

SelectEndpoint returns the endpoint with the highest security level that this client can actually use with its application instance certificate and that matches the security policy and mode. policy and mode can be omitted ("" and ua.MessageSecurityModeInvalid) so that only one of them, or neither, has to match.

The security level is the one the server advertises. Where a server gives several usable endpoints the same level (open62541 does, for all its ECC policies), the ranking of this library decides: see uapolicy.SecurityLevel. The policies with authenticated encryption come first.

It differs from ua.SelectEndpoint, which looks at the security level alone, in what it leaves out:

  - endpoints with a security policy this library does not implement,
  - secured endpoints whose policy does not fit the key of the certificate: a server that offers RSA and ECC endpoints ranks the ECC ones highest, but a client with an RSA certificate cannot use them (and a client with an ECC certificate cannot use the RSA ones),
  - all secured endpoints if certificate is empty.

certificate is the DER encoded application instance certificate of the client, as given to the Certificate option.

A server with opc.wss or opc.https endpoints next to opc.tcp ones returns all of them when the URL of the GetEndpoints request matches none exactly. SelectEndpoint then keeps to the opc.tcp endpoints, the transport of a client that has not asked for another one; with no opc.tcp endpoint in the list, every transport is considered, the UA Binary mappings before the UA JSON ones (wss-uajson, https-uajson), which a client uses only when asked to. SelectEndpointForTransport selects among the endpoints of one transport.

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {
	// endpointURL is the endpoint URL the client connects to.

	// cfg is the configuration for the client.

	// conn is the open connection

	// activeEndpoint is the endpoint URL of the current connection if it
	// differs from endpointURL and ownListener is the reverse connect
	// listener the client opened for itself. See reverse.go. Guarded by
	// connMu.

	// sechan is the open secure channel.
	// *uasc.SecureChannel

	// sechanErr receives the errors of the current secure channel. Every
	// secure channel gets its own channel (see Dial) so that an error of a
	// channel that has already been replaced cannot be mistaken for an error
	// of its successor. Guarded by connMu.

	// atomicSession is the active atomicSession.
	// *Session

	// leaving is the session ActivateSession is replacing: from the moment
	// it is being closed, faults of its requests are those of a session
	// the client has left, although it is still the active one until the
	// new session is set.

	// subMux guards subs and pendingAcks.

	// subs is the set of active subscriptions by id.

	// subGen counts the subscriptions registered so far; a Publish fault
	// for a request sent before the last registration is stale (see
	// markSubscriptionsBrokenSince). Guarded by subMux.

	// pendingAcks contains the pending subscription acknowledgements
	// for all active subscriptions.

	// subCreating counts the CreateSubscription requests of Subscribe whose
	// subscription is not registered yet, and subCreatesLost those requests
	// that failed without telling whether the server created the
	// subscription. See createSubscription.

	// lastPublishResponse is when the last Publish response arrived (unix
	// nanoseconds), see markSilentSubscriptions.

	// pausech pauses the subscription publish loop

	// resumech resumes subscription publish loop

	// publishPaused is the desired state of the publish loop and publishGen
	// counts how often it was resumed. See setPublishPaused.

	// subRecoverCh wakes the connection monitor when a subscription was
	// found to have ended on the server while the connection is fine. See
	// recoverBrokenSubscriptions.

	// deliverMu serialises the delivery of live PublishResponses with the
	// republishing done during a connection recovery.

	// mctx is the context of the connection monitor and the publish loop;
	// mcancel stops them. Both are created with the client so that Close and
	// Connect can be called concurrently.

	// monitorDone is closed when the connection monitor has stopped;
	// monitorStarted tells whether it was ever started. inMonitorHandler is
	// set while the monitor runs a user supplied handler and closeDone once
	// Close has finished. See Close.

	// timeout for sending PublishRequests
	// time.Duration

	// atomicState of the client
	// ConnState

	// stateCh is an optional channel for connection state changes. May be nil.

	// stateFunc is an optional func for connection state changes. May be nil.

	// recoveryFunc is an optional func called after each subscription recovery
	// attempt during automatic reconnect. May be nil.

	// list of cached atomicNamespaces on the server
	// []string

	// monitorOnce ensures only one connection monitor is running

}
```

Client is a high-level client for an OPC-UA server.

It manages the full connection lifecycle: establishing a TCP connection via UACP, opening a secure channel (UASC) with encryption and signing, creating and activating a session, and managing subscriptions.

The Client supports automatic reconnection when AutoReconnect is enabled. On connection loss it will attempt progressive recovery: recreating the secure channel, restoring or recreating the session, and transferring subscriptions.

Create a Client with [NewClient](#func-newclient) and connect with [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect). Always call [Client.Close](#func-client-close) when done to release resources.

The Client is safe for concurrent use from multiple goroutines.

```go
func NewClient(endpoint string, opts ...Option) (*Client, error)
```

NewClient creates a new Client.

When no options are provided the new client is created from DefaultClientConfig() and DefaultSessionConfig(). If no authentication method is configured, a UserIdentityToken for anonymous authentication will be set. See #Client.CreateSession for details.

To modify configuration you can provide any number of Options as opts. See #Option for details.

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close closes the session, secure channel, and underlying TCP connection.

It attempts to gracefully close the session on the server, then closes the secure channel and connection. Errors during session close are ignored to ensure cleanup completes.

Close is safe to call multiple times. After Close returns, the Client cannot be reused.

#### func (Client) Connect

```go
func (c *Client) Connect(ctx context.Context) error
```

Connect establishes a secure channel and creates a new session.

It performs the full OPC-UA connection sequence:

 1. Opens a TCP connection to the server (UACP)
 2. Opens a secure channel with the configured security policy
 3. Creates a session with the configured parameters
 4. Activates the session with the configured authentication

If AutoReconnect is enabled, Connect also starts a background goroutine that monitors the connection and attempts recovery on failure.

Connect must be called exactly once. Call [Client.Close](#func-client-close) to disconnect.

#### func (Client) FindServersOnNetworkWithFilter

```go
func (c *Client) FindServersOnNetworkWithFilter(ctx context.Context, startingRecordID, maxRecordsToReturn uint32, capabilityFilter []string) (*ua.FindServersOnNetworkResponse, error)
```

FindServersOnNetworkWithFilter calls FindServersOnNetwork with the parameters of the service (Part 4 §5.4.3). Only records with an id of at least startingRecordID are returned, at most maxRecordsToReturn of them (0 means no limit), and only servers that have all the capabilities in capabilityFilter. #### func (Client) HistoryReleaseContinuationPoints

```go
func (c *Client) HistoryReleaseContinuationPoints(ctx context.Context, details any, nodes ...*ua.HistoryReadValueID) ([]ua.StatusCode, error)
```

HistoryReleaseContinuationPoints releases the continuation points of HistoryRead calls the client does not continue: it sends a HistoryRead with releaseContinuationPoints set (Part 4 §5.10.3), which frees the points on the server and returns no history.

details are the HistoryReadDetails of the reads the points came from, a pointer to one of the HistoryReadDetails structures (Part 11 §6.5), e.g. \*ua.ReadRawModifiedDetails or \*ua.ReadEventDetails; nodes are the nodes with the continuation points to release. The result holds the status of each node in the order of nodes: Good when the point was released, Bad\_ContinuationPointInvalid for a point the server does not know (already used, released, expired, or of another session). Without nodes nothing is sent.


#### func (Client) NodeFromExpandedNodeID

```go
func (c *Client) NodeFromExpandedNodeID(id *ua.ExpandedNodeID) *Node
```

NodeFromExpandedNodeID returns a node object which accesses its attributes through this client connection. This is usually needed when working with node ids returned from browse responses by the server.

#### func (Client) NodeFromPath

```go
func (c *Client) NodeFromPath(ctx context.Context, path string) (*Node, error)
```

NodeFromPath resolves a dot-separated browse path to a Node.

Start node: server's Objects folder (i=85). Namespace: all path segments are interpreted in namespace 0. Path format: dot-separated browse names (e.g. "Server.ServerStatus"). Error behavior: returns (nil, err) if the path does not resolve, the TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs service fails, or the client is not connected. Use NodeFromPathInNamespace for a different namespace; use Node().TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID when starting from a custom node.

Example: NodeFromPath(ctx, "Server.ServerStatus") returns the ServerStatus node.

#### func (Client) NodeFromPathInNamespace

```go
func (c *Client) NodeFromPathInNamespace(ctx context.Context, ns uint16, path string) (*Node, error)
```

NodeFromPathInNamespace resolves a dot-separated browse path to a Node using a single namespace for all segments.

Start node: server's Objects folder (i=85). Namespace: all path segments use the given namespace index ns. Path format: dot-separated browse names (e.g. "MyFolder.Sensor1.Temperature"). Error behavior: returns (nil, err) if the path does not resolve, the service fails, or the client is not connected. For paths in namespace 0 from Objects folder, NodeFromPath is equivalent. For a custom start node, use Node().TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID.

Example: NodeFromPathInNamespace(ctx, 1, "Objects.IntVar") for a custom namespace 1.

#### func (Client) NodeFromQualifiedPath

```go
func (c *Client) NodeFromQualifiedPath(ctx context.Context, path string) (*Node, error)
```

NodeFromQualifiedPath resolves a namespace-qualified path to a Node.

Path format: dot-separated segments, each of the form "ns:name" where ns is a decimal namespace index (0-65535) and name is the browse name (e.g. "0:Server.0:ServerStatus" or "2:DeviceSet.4:PLC\_Name"). Parsing is protocol-level and uses TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs with per-segment namespace indices.

Start node: server's Objects folder (i=85). Namespace: each segment specifies its own namespace via the "ns:" prefix. Error behavior: returns (nil, err) if the path is invalid (e.g. segment missing "ns:" or ns not numeric), the path does not resolve, the service fails, or the client is not connected.

#### func (Client) ReadAlarmMetrics

```go
func (c *Client) ReadAlarmMetrics(ctx context.Context, metricsID *ua.NodeID) (*AlarmMetrics, error)
```

ReadAlarmMetrics reads the components of an AlarmMetricsType object. A component the object does not have (or that cannot be read) keeps its zero value; the error reports the first service failure.

#### func (Client) ReadEventHistory

```go
func (c *Client) ReadEventHistory(ctx context.Context, nodeID *ua.NodeID, start, end time.Time, filter *ua.EventFilter, maxEvents uint32) ([]*ua.HistoryEventFieldList, error)
```

ReadEventHistory reads the historical events of a HistoricalEventNode (an object or view with the HistoryRead bit of its EventNotifier, Part 11 §5.4.4) with Time in the range of start and end: the fields filter selects of the events that pass its WhereClause (Part 11 §6.5.2).

The events come oldest first, or newest first when start is after end (a reverse read). One of start and end may be the zero time when maxEvents is set: only start reads forward from start, only end reads backwards from end. maxEvents limits the number of events; 0 reads all events of the range. ReadEventHistory follows continuation points until it has maxEvents events or the history is exhausted, and releases the continuation point a server still holds for a truncated read.

A node with Good\_NoData returns no events and no error; a Bad status of the node is returned as the error (a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode)).

#### func (Client) ReadEventHistoryAll

```go
func (c *Client) ReadEventHistoryAll(ctx context.Context, nodeID *ua.NodeID, start, end time.Time, filter *ua.EventFilter, pageSize uint32) iter.Seq2[*ua.HistoryEventFieldList, error]
```

ReadEventHistoryAll returns an iterator over the historical events of a HistoricalEventNode with Time in the range of start and end, as [Client.ReadEventHistory](#func-client-readeventhistory) reads them, that follows continuation points as the consumer asks for more events. pageSize is the NumValuesPerNode of each HistoryRead: the most events one call returns (0 lets the server decide; it is required when start or end is the zero time).

When the consumer stops early, or ctx is done, while the server holds a continuation point for the read, the iterator releases it. A done ctx ends the iteration with ctx.Err(); when it cancelled a read in flight, the release is sent in the background, as the server may answer it only after the abandoned read.

#### func (Client) ReadHistory

```go
func (c *Client) ReadHistory(ctx context.Context, nodeID *ua.NodeID, start, end time.Time, maxValues uint32) ([]*ua.DataValue, error)
```

ReadHistory reads raw historical values for a single node within a time range. It returns up to maxValues results. Use maxValues=0 for all values in the range.

ReadHistory follows continuation points until it has maxValues values or the history is exhausted, and releases the continuation point a server still holds for a truncated read. A node with Good\_NoData returns no values and no error; a Bad status of the node is returned as the error (a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode)).

#### func (Client) ReadHistoryAll

```go
func (c *Client) ReadHistoryAll(ctx context.Context, nodeID *ua.NodeID, start, end time.Time) iter.Seq2[*ua.DataValue, error]
```

ReadHistoryAll returns an iterator that reads all historical data values for a node within the given time range, automatically following continuation points.

When the consumer stops early, or ctx is done, while the server holds a continuation point for the read, the iterator releases it. A done ctx ends the iteration with ctx.Err().

#### func (Client) ReadMulti

```go
func (c *Client) ReadMulti(ctx context.Context, items []ReadItem, opts ...ReadMultiOption) ([]ReadResult, error)
```

ReadMulti performs a batch read of N nodes × attributes in one or more OPC UA Read calls, chunking by DefaultReadMultiChunkSize (or chunkSize if provided via [ReadMultiWithChunkSize](#func-readmultiwithchunksize)). Results are in the same order as items. Each result's StatusCode reflects the server's status for that item; a failed overall request returns (nil, err).

#### func (Client) ReadValue

```go
func (c *Client) ReadValue(ctx context.Context, nodeID *ua.NodeID) (*ua.DataValue, error)
```

ReadValue reads the Value attribute of a single node.

This is a convenience wrapper around [Client.Read](#func-client-read) for the common case of reading one node's value. It returns timestamps from both source and server.

For reading multiple nodes in one round-trip, use [Client.ReadValues](#func-client-readvalues). For reading attributes other than Value, use [Client.Read](#func-client-read) directly.

#### func (Client) ReadValues

```go
func (c *Client) ReadValues(ctx context.Context, nodeIDs ...*ua.NodeID) ([]*ua.DataValue, error)
```

ReadValues reads the Value attribute of multiple nodes in a single request.

This is more efficient than calling [Client.ReadValue](#func-client-readvalue) in a loop because all nodes are read in a single OPC-UA Read service call. Results are returned in the same order as the input node IDs.

#### func (Client) RegisterNodes

```go
func (c *Client) RegisterNodes(ctx context.Context, req *ua.RegisterNodesRequest) (*ua.RegisterNodesResponse, error)
```

RegisterNodes registers node ids for more efficient reads.

Part 4, Section 5.8.5.

#### func (Client) RegisterServer

```go
func (c *Client) RegisterServer(ctx context.Context, server *ua.RegisteredServer) (*ua.RegisterServerResponse, error)
```

RegisterServer registers a server with the discovery server the client is connected to, renews its registration, or (server.IsOnline false) removes it (Part 4 §5.4.5).

The service needs a SecureChannel but no session: call [Client.Dial](#func-client-dial), not [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect). A discovery server normally only accepts registrations on a secured channel opened with the certificate of the server that is being registered.

A registration expires unless it is renewed; Part 4 recommends every 10 minutes. A go-opcua server does all of this by itself with server.WithDiscoveryRegistration.

#### func (Client) RegisterServer2

```go
func (c *Client) RegisterServer2(ctx context.Context, server *ua.RegisteredServer, configurations ...any) (*ua.RegisterServer2Response, error)
```

RegisterServer2 is RegisterServer with discovery configurations (Part 4 §5.4.6), typically one \*ua.MdnsDiscoveryConfiguration with the mDNS server name and the capabilities of the server. The response has one result per configuration: BadNotSupported means that the discovery server ignored that configuration; the server is registered nevertheless.

A discovery server that predates the service answers with BadServiceUnsupported (or BadNotSupported); use [Client.RegisterServer](#func-client-registerserver) then.

#### func (Client) Subscribe

```go
func (c *Client) Subscribe(ctx context.Context, params *SubscriptionParameters, notifyCh chan<- *PublishNotificationData) (*Subscription, error)
```

Subscribe creates a new OPC-UA subscription with the given parameters.

The subscription receives data change and event notifications from the server. Notifications are delivered to notifyCh. If the channel is full, the notification is dropped and counted in stats.

Parameters that have not been set use their defaults:

  - Interval: 100ms
  - LifetimeCount: 10000
  - MaxKeepAliveCount: 3000
  - MaxNotificationsPerPublish: 10000

The caller must call [Subscription.Cancel](#func-subscription-cancel) when done to clean up resources. For a fluent builder API, see [Client.NewSubscription](#func-client-newsubscription).

See OPC-UA Part 4, Section 5.13.1 for the specification.

### type ClientMetrics

```go
type ClientMetrics interface {
	// OnRequest is called before the request is sent to the server.
	// The service parameter is the OPC-UA service name (e.g. "Read", "Write",
	// "Browse", "Call", "CreateSubscription").
	OnRequest(service string)

	// OnResponse is called after a successful round-trip.
	OnResponse(service string, duration time.Duration)

	// OnError is called when a request fails with a non-timeout error.
	OnError(service string, duration time.Duration, err error)

	// OnTimeout is called when a request fails due to a timeout.
	OnTimeout(service string, duration time.Duration)
}
```

ClientMetrics receives callbacks for client-side OPC-UA service calls. All methods are called synchronously; implementations must be non-blocking (e.g. increment an atomic counter, send on a buffered channel).

Attach an implementation via [WithMetrics](#func-withmetrics).

### type ConditionEvent

```go
type ConditionEvent struct {
	ConditionID      *ua.NodeID
	EventID          []byte
	EventType        *ua.NodeID
	SourceNode       *ua.NodeID
	SourceName       string
	Time             time.Time
	Message          string
	Severity         uint16
	ConditionName    string
	ConditionClassID *ua.NodeID
	BranchID         *ua.NodeID
	Retain           bool
	Enabled          bool
	Quality          *ua.StatusCode
	LastSeverity     *uint16
	Comment          *ua.LocalizedText
	ClientUserID     string
	Acked            *bool
	Confirmed        *bool
	Active           *bool
	// SuppressedOrShelved and ShelvingState (the NodeId of the current
	// state of the ShelvedStateMachine) are those of an alarm.
	SuppressedOrShelved *bool
	ShelvingState       *ua.NodeID
	// Suppressed, OutOfService, Silenced and Latched are the optional
	// SuppressedState, OutOfServiceState, SilenceState and LatchedState of
	// an alarm (Part 9 §5.8.2); nil when the alarm does not have them.
	Suppressed   *bool
	OutOfService *bool
	Silenced     *bool
	Latched      *bool
	// DialogActive, Prompt and LastResponse are those of a dialog
	// (DialogConditionType, Part 9 §5.6).
	DialogActive *bool
	Prompt       *ua.LocalizedText
	LastResponse *int32
	// AudibleEnabled, ReAlarmRepeatCount and FirstInGroup are the optional
	// AudibleEnabled, ReAlarmRepeatCount and FirstInGroupFlag of an alarm
	// (Part 9 §5.8.2).
	AudibleEnabled     *bool
	ReAlarmRepeatCount *int16
	FirstInGroup       *bool
}
```

ConditionEvent is a condition event received through [NewConditionEventFilter](#func-newconditioneventfilter). The pointer fields are nil when the condition does not have the state (or reports it as Bad\_ConditionDisabled).

### type ConnState

```go
type ConnState uint8
```

ConnState represents the connection state of an OPC-UA [Client](#type-client).

Monitor state changes by providing a callback via [WithConnStateHandler](#func-withconnstatehandler).

```go
const (
	// Closed indicates the client is not connected. This is the initial state
	// and the final state after [Client.Close] or a failed reconnection.
	Closed ConnState = iota
	// Connected indicates the client has an active session and is ready for operations.
	Connected
	// Connecting indicates the client is establishing its first connection.
	Connecting
	// Disconnected indicates the connection was lost. If AutoReconnect is
	// enabled, the client will transition to Reconnecting.
	Disconnected
	// Reconnecting indicates the client is attempting to recover a lost connection.
	// On success it transitions to Connected; on failure to Closed.
	Reconnecting
)
```

### type DiscoveryResult

```go
type DiscoveryResult struct {
	// DiscoveryServerURL is the URL that was queried.
	DiscoveryServerURL string
	// Servers are the applications known to the discovery server
	// (FindServers): itself and the servers registered with it.
	Servers []*ua.ApplicationDescription
	// ServersOnNetwork are the servers the discovery server found on the
	// network with mDNS (FindServersOnNetwork). It is nil if the discovery
	// server does not have the multicast extension.
	ServersOnNetwork []*ua.ServerOnNetwork
	// LastCounterResetTime is when the record ids of ServersOnNetwork last
	// started over.
	LastCounterResetTime time.Time
	// MulticastSupported reports whether the discovery server answered
	// FindServersOnNetwork.
	MulticastSupported bool
}
```

DiscoveryResult is what a discovery server knows, as returned by [DiscoverServers](#func-discoverservers).

#### func DiscoverServers

```go
func DiscoverServers(ctx context.Context, host string, opts ...Option) (*DiscoveryResult, error)
```

DiscoverServers asks the Local Discovery Server of a host which servers it knows. host is a host name or IP address, to which the well-known discovery port 4840 is added (see [DiscoveryURL](#func-discoveryurl)), or a complete opc.tcp URL.

It calls FindServers and FindServersOnNetwork. The latter is optional: a discovery server without the multicast extension is not an error.

```go
func (n *Node) AccessLevel(ctx context.Context) (ua.AccessLevelType, error)
```

AccessLevel returns the access level of the node. The returned value is a mask where multiple values can be set, e.g. read and write.


#### func (Node) BrowseAll

```go
func (n *Node) BrowseAll(ctx context.Context, refType uint32, dir ua.BrowseDirection, mask ua.NodeClass, includeSubtypes bool) iter.Seq2[*ua.ReferenceDescription, error]
```

BrowseAll returns an iterator over all references for the node, automatically following continuation points. Results are streamed without accumulating in memory.

A Bad StatusCode of the BrowseResult or of a BrowseNext result (e.g. Bad\_NodeIdUnknown for an unknown node, Part 4 §5.8.2.2) is returned as the error, a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode).

#### func (Node) BrowseName

```go
func (n *Node) BrowseName(ctx context.Context) (*ua.QualifiedName, error)
```

BrowseName returns the browse name of the node.

#### func (Node) BrowseWithDepth

```go
func (n *Node) BrowseWithDepth(ctx context.Context, opts BrowseWithDepthOptions) ([]BrowseWithDepthResult, error)
```

BrowseWithDepth performs a client-side recursive browse from this node up to opts.MaxDepth, using the given reference type, direction, and node class filter. It returns a flat slice of references with their depth. Standard OPC UA Browse is single-level; this method implements recursion by issuing multiple Browse calls (same as [Node.WalkLimit](#func-node-walklimit) but returns a slice instead of an iterator). A Bad StatusCode of a Browse or BrowseNext result is returned as the error with the references collected so far.

#### func (Node) Children

```go
func (n *Node) Children(ctx context.Context, refs uint32, mask ua.NodeClass) ([]*Node, error)
```

Children returns the child nodes which match the node class mask.

A Bad StatusCode of the BrowseResult or of a BrowseNext result (e.g. Bad\_NodeIdUnknown for an unknown node, Part 4 §5.8.2.2) is returned as the error, a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode).




HasAccessLevel returns true if all bits from mask are set in the access level mask of the node.

```go

```

A Bad StatusCode of the BrowseResult or of a BrowseNext result (e.g. Bad\_NodeIdUnknown for an unknown node, Part 4 §5.8.2.2) is returned as the error, a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode).

```go
func (n *Node) References(ctx context.Context, refType uint32, dir ua.BrowseDirection, mask ua.NodeClass, includeSubtypes bool) ([]*ua.ReferenceDescription, error)
```

A Bad StatusCode of the BrowseResult or of a BrowseNext result (e.g. Bad\_NodeIdUnknown for an unknown node, Part 4 §5.8.2.2) is returned as the error, a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode).

```go
func (n *Node) String() string
```

#### func (Node) Summary

```go
func (n *Node) Summary(ctx context.Context) (*NodeSummary, error)
```

Summary reads the common attributes of the node in a single Read call and follows the HasTypeDefinition reference. This is the most efficient way to gather all display-relevant information about a node.

#### func (Node) TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID

```go
func (n *Node) TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID(ctx context.Context, ns uint16, browsePath string) (*ua.NodeID, error)
```

TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID resolves a dot-separated browse path to a NodeID, with all segments in one namespace.

Start node: the receiver node n. Namespace: every path segment uses the given namespace index ns. Path format: dot-separated browse names (e.g. "Server.ServerStatus" or "Sensors.Temperature"); split on "." and each segment becomes a QualifiedName{NamespaceIndex: ns, Name: segment}. Error behavior: returns (nil, err) if the path does not resolve, the TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs service fails, or the client is not connected. err may be a ua.StatusCode. For paths from the server's Objects folder, Client.NodeFromPath or Client.NodeFromPathInNamespace are simpler. For per-segment namespaces, use TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs with a \[]\*ua.QualifiedName.

#### func (Node) TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs

```go
func (n *Node) TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs(ctx context.Context, pathNames []*ua.QualifiedName) (*ua.NodeID, error)
```

TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs resolves a path of browse name segments to a single NodeID using the TranslateBrowsePathsToNodeIDs service.

Start node: the receiver node n (StartingNode in the request). Namespace: each segment can specify its own namespace via pathNames\[i].NamespaceIndex. Path format: slice of QualifiedName; traversal uses HierarchicalReferences. Error behavior: returns (nil, err) if the path does not resolve (no targets or non-OK status), the service fails, or the client is not connected. err may be a ua.StatusCode (e.g. StatusBadNotFound). For a dot-separated path string with one namespace for all segments, use TranslateBrowsePathInNamespaceToNodeID.

#### func (Node) TypeDefinition

```go
func (n *Node) TypeDefinition(ctx context.Context) (*ua.NodeID, error)
```

TypeDefinition returns the NodeID of the type definition for this node by following the HasTypeDefinition reference. A node without one gives (nil, nil); an unknown node gives the Bad StatusCode of the Browse result (Bad\_NodeIdUnknown).

#### func (Node) UserAccessLevel

```go
func (n *Node) UserAccessLevel(ctx context.Context) (ua.AccessLevelType, error)
```

UserAccessLevel returns the access level of the node.

#### func (Node) Value

```go
func (n *Node) Value(ctx context.Context) (*ua.Variant, error)
```

Value returns the value of the node.

#### func (Node) Walk

```go
func (n *Node) Walk(ctx context.Context) iter.Seq2[WalkResult, error]
```

Walk returns an iterator that recursively descends through the node's hierarchical references, yielding each discovered reference along with its depth. The walk uses BrowseAll to automatically follow continuation points. For a depth limit, use WalkLimit.

A Bad StatusCode of a Browse or BrowseNext result, of the start node or of a node the walk descends into, is yielded as the error (a [ua.StatusCode](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusCode)) and ends the walk. Targets on other servers (ServerIndex != 0) are yielded but not descended into.

#### func (Node) WalkLimit

```go
func (n *Node) WalkLimit(ctx context.Context, maxDepth int) iter.Seq2[WalkResult, error]
```

WalkLimit is like Walk but stops recursing when depth reaches maxDepth. The node at depth maxDepth is still yielded. If maxDepth \< 0, depth is unlimited. Use this for "find node", "find type", or "browse tree" style tools to avoid unbounded traversal (e.g. pass a -depth flag from the CLI).

The same node may be yielded more than once if it is reachable via multiple hierarchical paths. Use WalkLimitDedup to yield each node at most once.

#### func (Node) WalkLimitDedup

```go
func (n *Node) WalkLimitDedup(ctx context.Context, maxDepth int) iter.Seq2[WalkResult, error]
```

WalkLimitDedup is like WalkLimit but yields each node at most once, keyed by NodeID. When a node is reachable via multiple hierarchical paths, only the first occurrence (by traversal order) is yielded. Use this to avoid duplicate nodes without implementing a visited set in the caller.

```go
}
```

NodeSummary contains the common attributes of a node, read in a single round-trip via [Node.Summary](#func-node-summary).

```go

```

ApplicationURI sets the application uri in the session configuration.

#### func AuthAnonymous

```go
func AuthAnonymous() Option
```

The policy ID is typically set via SecurityFromEndpoint. It can also be set explicitly with AuthPolicyID (in any order).

#### func AuthCertificate

```go
func AuthCertificate(cert []byte) Option
```

AuthCertificate sets the authentication mode to X509 certificate.

The policy ID is typically set via SecurityFromEndpoint. It can also be set explicitly with AuthPolicyID (in any order).

#### func AuthIssuedToken

```go

```

AuthIssuedToken sets the authentication mode to an externally-issued token.

tokenData is the opaque token value whose format depends on the token type advertised by the server's UserTokenPolicy (e.g. SAML, JWT, WS-Security). See OPC-UA Part 4, §7.36.6 for details on IssuedIdentityToken encoding.

The policy ID is typically set via SecurityFromEndpoint. It can also be set explicitly with AuthPolicyID (in any order).

#### func AuthPolicyID

```go
func AuthPolicyID(policy string) Option
```

AuthPolicyID sets the policy ID of the user identity token.

This can be called before or after an AuthXXX method. If called before, the policy ID is stored and applied once the token type is set.

Most callers should use SecurityFromEndpoint which automatically determines the correct policy ID from the endpoint description.

#### func AuthPrivateKey

```go
func AuthPrivateKey(key *rsa.PrivateKey) Option
```

AuthPrivateKey sets the client's authentication RSA private key Note: PolicyID still needs to be set outside of this method, typically through the SecurityFromEndpoint() Option.

For the key of an ECC user certificate use AuthPrivateKeySigner.

#### func AuthPrivateKeySigner

```go
func AuthPrivateKeySigner(key crypto.Signer) Option
```

AuthPrivateKeySigner sets the private key of the user certificate given with AuthCertificate. It accepts every supported key type: an \*rsa.PrivateKey, or a crypto.Signer with an ECDSA, Ed25519 or Ed448 public key when the user token is protected with an ECC security policy (Ed25519 for ECC\_curve25519, Ed448 for ECC\_curve448, ECDSA for the others).

#### func AuthUsername

```go
func AuthUsername(user, pass string) Option
```

AuthUsername sets the authentication mode to username/password.

The policy ID is typically set via SecurityFromEndpoint. It can also be set explicitly with AuthPolicyID (in any order).

#### func AutoReconnect

```go
func AutoReconnect(b bool) Option
```

AutoReconnect sets the auto reconnect state of the secure channel.

#### func Certificate

```go
func Certificate(cert []byte) Option
```

Certificate sets the client X509 certificate in the secure channel configuration. It also detects and sets the ApplicationURI from the URI within the certificate.

#### func CertificateFile

```go
func CertificateFile(filename string) Option
```

CertificateFile sets the client X509 certificate in the secure channel configuration from the PEM or DER encoded file. It also detects and sets the ApplicationURI from the URI within the certificate.

#### func DialTimeout

```go
func DialTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

DialTimeout sets the timeout for establishing the UACP connection. Defaults to DefaultDialTimeout. Set to zero for no timeout.

#### func Dialer

```go
func Dialer(d *uacp.Dialer) Option
```

Dialer sets the uacp.Dialer to establish the connection to the server.

#### func HTTPClient

```go
func HTTPClient(c *http.Client) Option
```

HTTPClient sets the HTTP client that posts the requests to an opc.https endpoint, for a proxy or transport of the application's own. Without it the client uses uasc.NewHTTPSClient with the TLSConfig option. It must not time requests out on its own: a Publish request waits on the server.

#### func HTTPSJSONContentType

```go
func HTTPSJSONContentType(contentType string) Option
```

HTTPSJSONContentType sets the Content-Type of the requests over https-uajson (TransportProfile ua.TransportProfileHTTPSJSON). The default is uasc.HTTPSJSONContentType, application/json (Part 6 §7.4.2); uasc.HTTPSJSONContentTypeLegacy, application/opcua+uajson, reaches servers that take only that one, such as UA-.NETStandard 2.0.1.

#### func InsecureNoSecurity

```go
func InsecureNoSecurity() Option
```

InsecureNoSecurity connects without message security: security policy None and security mode None. Messages are neither signed nor encrypted and the server is not authenticated, so anyone on the network path can read and change them, and any password sent is exposed.

A client refuses to run this way unless this option is given (errors.ErrInsecureNotAllowed), also when policy None comes from [SecurityPolicy](#func-securitypolicy), [SecurityMode](#func-securitymode) or an endpoint given to [SecurityFromEndpoint](#func-securityfromendpoint). Not needed for the discovery services [GetEndpoints](#func-getendpoints), [FindServers](#func-findservers) and [FindServersOnNetwork](#func-findserversonnetwork), which the specification defines without security, or for transports secured by TLS (opc.https, opc.wss).

#### func InsecureSkipVerify

```go
func InsecureSkipVerify() Option
```

InsecureSkipVerify disables server certificate validation. When set, the client still parses the server certificate to extract the public key (required for signing and encryption), but does not verify the trust chain, expiration, or application URI.

This is INSECURE and should only be used for development and testing.

#### func Lifetime

```go
func Lifetime(d time.Duration) Option
```

Lifetime sets the lifetime of the secure channel in milliseconds. The RequestedLifetime is a UInt32 (Part 4 §5.5.2.2): a negative duration is sent as 0 and one longer than about 49.7 days as the largest value.

#### func Locales

```go
func Locales(locale ...string) Option
```

Locales sets the locales in the session configuration.

#### func MaxChunkCount

```go
func MaxChunkCount(n uint32) Option
```

MaxChunkCount sets the maximum chunk count for the UACP handshake: the most chunks of a response the client accepts (Part 6 §7.1.2.3). As with MaxMessageSize, 0 takes the server's limit, or uacp.DefaultMaxChunkCount.

#### func MaxMessageSize

```go
func MaxMessageSize(n uint32) Option
```

MaxMessageSize sets the maximum message size for the UACP handshake: the largest response body the client accepts (Part 6 §7.1.2.3). The client accepts no more than this even if the server announces a larger limit; 0, the default, takes the server's limit, or uacp.DefaultMaxMessageSize when the server has none.

#### func PrivateKey

```go
func PrivateKey(key *rsa.PrivateKey) Option
```

PrivateKey sets the RSA private key in the secure channel configuration.

For the key of an ECC application instance certificate use PrivateKeySigner.

#### func PrivateKeyFile

```go
func PrivateKeyFile(filename string) Option
```

PrivateKeyFile sets the private key in the secure channel configuration from a PEM or DER encoded file. The key is an RSA key (PKCS #1 or PKCS #8) an ECDSA key on a NIST or Brainpool curve (PKCS #8 or SEC 1 "EC PRIVATE KEY") or an Ed25519 or Ed448 key (PKCS #8).

#### func PrivateKeySigner

```go
func PrivateKeySigner(key crypto.Signer) Option
```

PrivateKeySigner sets the private key of the client's application instance certificate. It accepts every supported key type: an \*rsa.PrivateKey for the RSA security policies, an ECDSA key (P-256 or P-384) for the ECC security policies ECC\_nistP256, ECC\_nistP384, ECC\_nistP256\_AesGcm and ECC\_nistP256\_ChaChaPoly, an Ed25519 key for ECC\_curve25519, an ECDSA key on brainpoolP256r1 or brainpoolP384r1 for ECC\_brainpoolP256r1 and ECC\_brainpoolP384r1, and an Ed448 key (github.com/cloudflare/circl/sign/ ed448) for ECC\_curve448.

An ECC key only has to sign, so it may be any crypto.Signer with an ECDSA, Ed25519 or Ed448 public key, for example a key held in an HSM. An RSA key also decrypts and must be an \*rsa.PrivateKey.


ProductURI sets the product uri in the session configuration.


RandomRequestID assigns a random initial request id.

The request id is generated using the 'rand' package and it is the caller's responsibility to initialize the random number generator properly.

#### func ReceiveBufferSize

```go
func ReceiveBufferSize(n uint32) Option
```

ReceiveBufferSize sets the receive buffer size for the UACP handshake.

```go
func ReconnectInterval(d time.Duration) Option
```

ReconnectInterval is interval duration between each reconnection attempt.

#### func RemoteCertificate

```go
func RemoteCertificate(cert []byte) Option
```

RemoteCertificate sets the server certificate.

#### func RemoteCertificateFile

```go
func RemoteCertificateFile(filename string) Option
```

RemoteCertificateFile sets the server certificate from the file in PEM or DER encoding.

#### func RequestTimeout

```go
func RequestTimeout(t time.Duration) Option
```

RequestTimeout sets the timeout for all requests over SecureChannel.

#### func ReturnDiagnostics

```go
func ReturnDiagnostics(mask uint32) Option
```

ReturnDiagnostics sets the ReturnDiagnostics mask of the RequestHeader of every request the client sends (Part 4 §7.33), e.g. ua.ReturnDiagnosticsAll. A request that sets a mask of its own keeps it.

The server then returns DiagnosticInfos: the operation diagnostics are in the DiagnosticInfos of the response (resolve them with ResponseHeader.Diagnostic), and a request the server rejects fails with a \*ServiceError that carries the service diagnostics and unwraps to the StatusCode.

#### func ReverseConnect

```go
func ReverseConnect(listenAddr string, opts ...ReverseConnectOption) Option
```

ReverseConnect makes the client wait for the server to connect to it instead of connecting to the server (OPC UA reverse connect, Part 6 §7.1.3). It is meant for servers the client cannot reach, for example because they sit behind a firewall or NAT, but which can reach the client.

The client listens on listenAddr, a "host:port" address or an "opc.tcp://host:port" URL, from the first [Client.Connect](#func-client-connect) (or [Client.Dial](#func-client-dial)) until [Client.Close](#func-client-close). The server must be configured with the address the client is reachable at; see server.WithReverseConnect for a server of this module.

The server announces itself with a ReverseHello message that carries its ServerUri and the EndpointUrl the client is to use. The client refuses the connection, and keeps waiting, unless

  - the ServerUri is the one set with [ReverseServerURI](#func-reverseserveruri), if any, and
  - the EndpointUrl denotes the endpoint URL the client was created with (see [NewClient](#func-newclient)). A client created with an empty endpoint URL accepts any EndpointUrl and uses it.

A ReverseHello message is not authenticated: anyone who can reach the listener can send one with any content. The server is authenticated, as always, by its certificate when the secure channel is opened, so use a security mode other than None and validate the server certificate. The client then also requires the ServerUri to be the ApplicationUri of the certificate it is configured with (unless [InsecureSkipVerify](#func-insecureskipverify) is set).

The time the client waits for the server is bounded by the context passed to Connect and by [DialTimeout](#func-dialtimeout). Servers typically retry a reverse connection only every few seconds, so the timeout must be long enough to cover one such interval. With [AutoReconnect](#func-autoreconnect) the client goes back to waiting for the server after a connection loss and restores the session and the subscriptions as usual.

The discovery helpers [GetEndpoints](#func-getendpoints), [FindServers](#func-findservers) and [FindServersOnNetwork](#func-findserversonnetwork) accept the option as well. To serve several servers or clients with one listener use [ReverseConnectListener](#func-reverseconnectlistener).

#### func ReverseConnectListener

```go
func ReverseConnectListener(l *uacp.ReverseListener, opts ...ReverseConnectOption) Option
```

ReverseConnectListener is like [ReverseConnect](#func-reverseconnect) but makes the client take its reverse connection from l instead of opening a listener of its own.

One listener can be shared by any number of clients, which is how several servers are served on a single port: give every client the ServerUri of its server with [ReverseServerURI](#func-reverseserveruri). The listener hands each incoming connection to the client that expects it and keeps a connection nobody is waiting for until a client asks for it.

Create the listener with uacp.ListenReverse or, for a net.Listener of your own, uacp.NewReverseListener; its configuration bounds the number of pending connections and can restrict the servers that are admitted at all. The listener is not closed by [Client.Close](#func-client-close): close it yourself once all its clients are closed.


SecurityFromEndpoint sets the server-related security parameters from a chosen endpoint (received from GetEndpoints()).

#### func SkipNamespaceUpdate

```go
func SkipNamespaceUpdate() Option
```

SkipNamespaceUpdate disables automatic namespace table update on connect and reconnect. Use this when the server does not support namespace queries. See [https://github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pull/512](https://github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pull/512) for discussion.

#### func TLSConfig

```go
func TLSConfig(c *tls.Config) Option
```

TLSConfig sets the TLS configuration of opc.wss (Part 6 §7.5) and opc.https (Part 6 §7.4) endpoints: RootCAs, the roots the server's TLS certificate is verified against (nil for the system roots), a client TLS certificate for servers that require one, ServerName. The TLS certificates are separate from the application instance certificates, which secure the session as on opc.tcp. TLS 1.2 is the minimum version. A uacp.Dialer given with the Dialer option keeps its own TLSConfig if it has one.

#### func TransportProfile

```go
func TransportProfile(uri string) Option
```

TransportProfile selects the transport mapping of the endpoint by its TransportProfileUri (Part 7). The URL scheme selects the transport, and by default its UA Binary mapping; ua.TransportProfileHTTPSJSON (an opc.https endpoint, Part 6 §7.4.5) and ua.TransportProfileWSSJSON (an opc.wss endpoint, Part 6 §7.5.2) select its UA JSON mapping instead, where every service message is a JSON message without secure conversation. A JSON profile whose scheme is not that of the endpoint URL fails Dial with errors.ErrInvalidEndpoint. SecurityFromEndpoint sets the profile of the endpoint it is given, so that selecting a wss-uajson or https-uajson endpoint with SelectEndpointForTransport is enough.

#### func TrustedCertificates

```go
func TrustedCertificates(certs ...*x509.Certificate) Option
```

TrustedCertificates adds the CA or self-signed certificates a server certificate is validated against: the application trust list (Part 4 §6.1.3). Nothing else is trusted, the system CA pool included, so a client using message security needs this option or [InsecureSkipVerify](#func-insecureskipverify).

Use this to trust self-signed server certificates or private CAs without disabling all validation via InsecureSkipVerify. Parse certificates with Brainpool or Ed448 keys, which crypto/x509 rejects, with uapolicy.ParseCertificate.

#### func WithConnStateChan

```go
func WithConnStateChan(ch chan<- ConnState) Option
```

WithConnStateChan sets a channel for receiving client connection state changes. The caller must provide a buffered channel and consume it promptly to prevent blocking. Sends are context-aware: if the context is cancelled, the state change is dropped rather than blocking.

#### func WithConnStateHandler

```go
func WithConnStateHandler(h func(ConnState)) Option
```

WithConnStateHandler sets a callback for receiving client connection state changes.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger for the client. By default logging is disabled (silent discard handler). Pass nil to restore the silent default.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m ClientMetrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets a metrics callback handler for the client. All methods are called synchronously; implementations must be non-blocking.

#### func WithRetryPolicy

```go
func WithRetryPolicy(p RetryPolicy) Option
```

WithRetryPolicy sets the retry policy for failed client requests. By default no retries are performed.

Example:

	// Retry up to 4 times with exponential back-off.
	opcua.WithRetryPolicy(opcua.ExponentialBackoff(200*time.Millisecond, 5*time.Second, 4))

#### func WithSubscriptionRecoveryHandler

```go
func WithSubscriptionRecoveryHandler(h func(SubscriptionRecoveryEvent)) Option
```

WithSubscriptionRecoveryHandler sets a callback that is invoked once per subscription after each automatic reconnect recovery attempt.

The handler is called synchronously from the reconnect goroutine and must not block. It receives a [SubscriptionRecoveryEvent](#type-subscriptionrecoveryevent) describing the outcome for each subscription: whether it was transferred, republished, recreated, partially recovered, or lost due to an unrecoverable gap.

This mirrors the [WithConnStateHandler](#func-withconnstatehandler) pattern and is the recommended way to implement observability for subscription recovery without polling.

### type PublishNotificationData

```go
type PublishNotificationData struct {
	SubscriptionID uint32
	Error          error
	Value          ua.Notification
}
```

PublishNotificationData contains a notification received from a subscription.

Check Error first — if non-nil, Value will be nil. When Error is nil, Value contains the notification which can be a [\*ua.DataChangeNotification](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#DataChangeNotification), [\*ua.EventNotificationList](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#EventNotificationList), or [\*ua.StatusChangeNotification](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusChangeNotification).

### type RetryPolicy

```go
type RetryPolicy interface {
	// ShouldRetry is called after each failed attempt.
	// attempt is zero-based (0 = first failure).
	// Return (true, delay) to retry after delay, or (false, 0) to stop.
	ShouldRetry(attempt int, err error) (bool, time.Duration)
}
```

RetryPolicy controls retry behaviour for failed client requests. The policy is consulted after each failed attempt to determine whether to retry and how long to wait before the next attempt.

Attach an implementation via [WithRetryPolicy](#func-withretrypolicy).

#### func ExponentialBackoff

```go
func ExponentialBackoff(base, maxDelay time.Duration, maxAttempts int) RetryPolicy
```

ExponentialBackoff returns a RetryPolicy with exponential back-off. delay = base × 2^attempt, capped at maxDelay. Stops after maxAttempts retries. maxAttempts = 0 means unlimited (always pair with a context deadline).

#### func NewExponentialBackoff

```go
func NewExponentialBackoff(cfg ExponentialBackoffConfig) RetryPolicy
```

NewExponentialBackoff returns a RetryPolicy with full control over the exponential back-off parameters via ExponentialBackoffConfig.

#### func NoRetry

```go
func NoRetry() RetryPolicy
```

NoRetry returns a RetryPolicy that never retries (default behaviour).

### type ReverseConnectOption

```go
type ReverseConnectOption func(*reverseConfig)
```

ReverseConnectOption configures the reverse connect behaviour of a client. See [ReverseConnect](#func-reverseconnect) and [ReverseConnectListener](#func-reverseconnectlistener).

#### func ReverseServerURI

```go
func ReverseServerURI(uri string) ReverseConnectOption
```

ReverseServerURI makes the client accept a reverse connection only from the server that announces uri as its ServerUri, which is the server's ApplicationUri.

It is required to tell servers apart when several of them connect to the same listener (see [ReverseConnectListener](#func-reverseconnectlistener)) and recommended otherwise. Note that the announcement alone proves nothing: see [ReverseConnect](#func-reverseconnect).

### type Session

```go
type Session struct {

	// activateMu serializes the ActivateSession calls of the session: the
	// reconnect logic and the application can activate it at the same time,
	// and each activation uses the nonce and the ephemeral key the previous
	// one brought.

	// resp is the response to the CreateSession request which contains all
	// necessary parameters to activate the session.

	// serverCertificate is the certificate used to generate the signatures for
	// the ActivateSessionRequest methods

	// serverNonce is the secret nonce received from the server during Create and Activate
	// Session response. Used to generate the signatures for the ActivateSessionRequest
	// and User Authorization

	// clientNonce is the nonce sent in the CreateSession request. The channel
	// bound signatures of ActivateSession cover it.

	// serverEphemeralKey is the ephemeral public key the server handed out
	// most recently, for user identity tokens that are protected with an ECC
	// security policy. A key is used for one ActivateSession only; every
	// response brings the key for the next one.

	// revisedTimeout is the actual maximum time that a Session shall remain open without activity.

}
```

Session is a OPC/UA session as described in Part 4, 5.6.

### type Subscription

```go
type Subscription struct {
	SubscriptionID            uint32
	RevisedPublishingInterval time.Duration
	RevisedLifetimeCount      uint32
	RevisedMaxKeepAliveCount  uint32
	Notifs                    chan<- *PublishNotificationData

	// see stableItemIDNeedsLock; guarded by itemsMu

	// idMu guards SubscriptionID, which changes when the subscription is
	// recreated after a reconnect while other goroutines use it. Code in
	// this package reads it through id().

	// needsRecreate is set when recreating the subscription after a
	// reconnect failed. The next recovery then recreates it instead of
	// trying to transfer and republish it. Guarded by Client.subMux.

	// lastActivity is when the server last sent a message for the
	// subscription (unix nanoseconds), or when the client last had reason
	// to start counting anew. See Client.markSilentSubscriptions.

	// session is the session the client last put the subscription in: the
	// one it was created in, or the one the client transferred it to. A
	// Good_SubscriptionTransferred from another session is not news: the
	// client moved the subscription itself.

	// cancelled is closed by Cancel. It releases a notification that is
	// being handed to Notifs: the consumer of a cancelled subscription
	// usually stops reading, and the client's single publish loop must not
	// block on it forever.

}
```

Subscription represents an active OPC-UA subscription on the server.

A subscription receives periodic notifications about data changes and events from monitored items. Notifications are delivered to the Notifs channel.

Create a subscription with [Client.Subscribe](#func-client-subscribe) or [SubscriptionBuilder.Start](#func-subscriptionbuilder-start). Add monitored items with [Subscription.Monitor](#func-subscription-monitor). Call [Subscription.Cancel](#func-subscription-cancel) when done to clean up resources on both client and server.

The RevisedPublishingInterval, RevisedLifetimeCount, and RevisedMaxKeepAliveCount fields contain the values negotiated with the server, which may differ from the requested values.

#### func (Subscription) Cancel

```go
func (s *Subscription) Cancel(ctx context.Context) error
```

Cancel stops the subscription and removes it from the client and the server.


ConditionRefresh calls ConditionRefresh for the subscription.



#### func (Subscription) Monitor

```go
func (s *Subscription) Monitor(ctx context.Context, ts ua.TimestampsToReturn, items ...*ua.MonitoredItemCreateRequest) (*ua.CreateMonitoredItemsResponse, error)
```

Monitor creates monitored items on the server for data change or event notifications. If the server closes the connection (e.g. because it does not support event or alarm subscriptions), the returned error wraps io.EOF with a message suggesting that the server may not support event or alarm subscriptions; callers can use errors.Is(err, io.EOF).

The MonitoredItemID of each result stays valid for the life of the subscription: [Subscription.Unmonitor](#func-subscription-unmonitor), [Subscription.ModifyMonitoredItems](#func-subscription-modifymonitoreditems), [Subscription.SetMonitoringMode](#func-subscription-setmonitoringmode) and [Subscription.SetTriggering](#func-subscription-settriggering) accept it even after the subscription was recreated on the server following a reconnect, when the server knows the item by a new id. For that reason the id can differ from the one on the wire.

#### func (Subscription) SetMonitoringMode

```go

```

```go
func (s *Subscription) SetPublishingMode(ctx context.Context, publishingEnabled bool) (*ua.SetPublishingModeResponse, error)
```

SetPublishingMode enables or disables publishing of notification messages for this subscription.

Part 4, Section 5.13.4.

#### func (Subscription) SetTriggering

```go
func (s *Subscription) SetTriggering(ctx context.Context, triggeringItemID uint32, add, remove []uint32) (*ua.SetTriggeringResponse, error)
```

SetTriggering sends a request to the server to add and/or remove triggering links from a triggering item. To add links from a triggering item to an item to report provide the ID(s) returned by Monitor in the \`add\` argument. To remove links from a triggering item to an item to report provide the ID(s) returned by Monitor in the \`remove\` argument.

#### func (Subscription) Stats

```go
func (s *Subscription) Stats(ctx context.Context) (*ua.SubscriptionDiagnosticsDataType, error)
```

Stats returns a diagnostic struct with metadata about the current subscription.

This reads the full SubscriptionDiagnosticsArray from the server and filters by SubscriptionID. A future optimisation could browse for the specific diagnostics node (e.g. i=2290/\<subscription-guid>) and cache its NodeID, but the current approach works with all servers regardless of how they structure the diagnostics address space.

```go

```

### type SubscriptionBuilder

```go
type SubscriptionBuilder struct {

	// if > 0, applied to Monitor/MonitorEvents items (server-side sampling rate in ms)

}
```

SubscriptionBuilder provides a fluent API for constructing and starting subscriptions with monitored items.

Create a builder with [Client.NewSubscription](#func-client-newsubscription) and chain configuration methods. Call [SubscriptionBuilder.Start](#func-subscriptionbuilder-start) to create the subscription on the server:

	sub, ch, err := c.NewSubscription().
	    Interval(100 * time.Millisecond).
	    Monitor(nodeID1, nodeID2).
	    Start(ctx)

If no notification channel is set via [SubscriptionBuilder.NotifyChannel](#func-subscriptionbuilder-notifychannel), Start creates a buffered channel with capacity 256.

#### func (SubscriptionBuilder) DataChangeFilter

```go
func (b *SubscriptionBuilder) DataChangeFilter(trigger ua.DataChangeTrigger, deadbandType ua.DeadbandType, deadbandValue float64) *SubscriptionBuilder
```

DataChangeFilter sets the data-change filter of the items added by subsequent Monitor calls: which changes are reported (trigger) and how far a numeric value has to move away from the last reported one (deadband). See [NewDataChangeFilter](#func-newdatachangefilter) for the parameters. Call it before Monitor; items added earlier, MonitorItems and MonitorEvents are not affected.

	sub, ch, err := c.NewSubscription().
	    DataChangeFilter(ua.DataChangeTriggerStatusValue, ua.DeadbandTypeAbsolute, 0.5).
	    Monitor(nodeID).
	    Start(ctx)


Interval sets the requested publishing interval.

LifetimeCount sets the requested lifetime count.

MonitorEvents adds event-monitoring items for the given node IDs using the provided EventFilter. Each node is monitored on AttributeIDEventNotifier.

NotifyChannel sets the channel for receiving notifications. If not set, Start creates a buffered channel with capacity 256.


Priority sets the subscription priority.

#### func (SubscriptionBuilder) SamplingInterval

```go
func (b *SubscriptionBuilder) SamplingInterval(d time.Duration) *SubscriptionBuilder
```

SamplingInterval sets the requested sampling interval for monitored items added by Monitor or MonitorEvents. The server samples at this rate (in milliseconds); the subscription's publishing interval controls how often notifications are sent to the client. If not set or zero, the server uses the fastest practical rate (0.0 in OPC UA). Call this before Monitor or MonitorEvents to apply to those items.


Start creates the subscription and monitored items on the server. It returns the subscription and the notification channel. If the server closes the connection during creation, the error may wrap io.EOF with a message suggesting the server may not support subscriptions or event/alarm monitoring.

### type SubscriptionParameters

```go
type SubscriptionParameters struct {
	Interval                   time.Duration
	LifetimeCount              uint32
	MaxKeepAliveCount          uint32

}
```

SubscriptionParameters configures a subscription's behavior.

Fields that are left at their zero value will use the defaults:

  - Interval: 100ms
  - LifetimeCount: 10000
  - MaxKeepAliveCount: 3000

### type SubscriptionRecoveryEvent

```go
type SubscriptionRecoveryEvent struct {
	// SubscriptionID is the OPC UA subscription identifier on the server.
	SubscriptionID uint32

	// Outcome describes the recovery result for this subscription.
	Outcome SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome

	// AvailableSequenceNumbers contains the sequence numbers that the server
	// reported as available for retransmission at the time of recovery.
	// It is empty when the subscription was recreated or transfer failed.
	AvailableSequenceNumbers []uint32

	// Detail is a human-readable description of the outcome, suitable for
	// logging or display. It is never empty.
	Detail string
}
```

SubscriptionRecoveryEvent is delivered to the handler registered via [WithSubscriptionRecoveryHandler](#func-withsubscriptionrecoveryhandler) after each subscription recovery attempt during automatic reconnect.

### type SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome

```go
type SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome string
```

SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome describes what happened to a subscription during automatic reconnect recovery.

```go
const (
	// SubscriptionRecoveryTransferred means the subscription was successfully
	// transferred to the new session and all expected messages were republished.
	SubscriptionRecoveryTransferred SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome = "transferred"

	// SubscriptionRecoveryRepublished means some or all buffered notifications
	// were recovered via Republish after a successful TransferSubscriptions.
	SubscriptionRecoveryRepublished SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome = "republished"

	// SubscriptionRecoveryRecreated means the subscription could not be
	// transferred and was recreated as a new subscription on the server.
	SubscriptionRecoveryRecreated SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome = "recreated"

	// SubscriptionRecoveryPartial means recovery was only partially successful:
	// some sequence numbers were republished but a gap remains.
	SubscriptionRecoveryPartial SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome = "partially_recovered"

	// SubscriptionRecoveryUnrecoverableGap means the client's expected next
	// sequence number is not present in the server's retransmission buffer;
	// notifications between the last delivered message and the oldest buffered
	// message are permanently lost.
	SubscriptionRecoveryUnrecoverableGap SubscriptionRecoveryOutcome = "unrecoverable_gap"
)
```

```go
type WalkResult struct {
```
